advances:
The registered profile inequality is false.  An exact full-dimensional
\(\ell_\infty\)-radial double cone in base dimension two and continuous
dimension ten satisfies the strict singleton condition, every strict
primitive-line condition, the marginal \(W/4\) condition at an interior
lattice anchor, and
\[
Q^\circ>\frac{16-e}{256}W^2.
\]
Nevertheless, every support-safe \(\Psi\)-term centered at that anchor is
exactly zero, and the anchor term is strictly less than \(W/64\).

This isolates the midpoint-synchronization failure.  The off-diagonal
quantity \(Q^\circ\) counts same-parity pairs over all integer midpoints.  In
this body it is large, but the pairs with the prescribed marginal
centerpoint as midpoint all lie below the support-safe budget.  Thus the
accepted parity-midpoint and fiber-capacity interfaces cannot localize the
global parity energy to the \(\Psi\)-score at the marginal centerpoint.
Unlike the accepted flat-pair obstruction, this is already an exact
\(n=2\) obstruction and uses the complete support-safe score, not a
flatness eligibility restriction.

proof:
The function
\[
(z,x)\longmapsto\|z\|_\infty+\|x\|_2
\]
is a norm on \(\mathbb R^{12}\).  Hence (1) is compact, convex, and has
nonempty interior.  Fixing \(z\) gives the Euclidean ball in (3), with
radius \((21-\|z\|_\infty)_+\).  A radius-zero fiber has zero
ten-dimensional volume.  This proves the complete profile (2) and (3).

For \(1\leq m\leq20\), the lattice shell
\[
\{z\in\mathbb Z^2:\|z\|_\infty=m\}
\]
has exactly \(8m\) points.  Summing (3) over the shells proves (4).

We first check the strict singleton condition.  The largest fiber is the
anchor fiber,
\[
w_0=\omega_{10}21^{10},
\qquad
21^{10}=16679880978201.
\]
The exact difference
\[
\overline W-4\cdot21^{10}
=384761062540197>0
\tag{6}
\]
therefore proves
\[
w_z\leq w_0<\frac W4
\qquad(z\in\mathbb Z^2).
\]

We next check every primitive rank-one coset.  If such a coset meets
\(\mathbb Z^2\), enumerate its lattice points as
\[
a+kv,\qquad k\in\mathbb Z,
\]
where \(v\in\mathbb Z^2\setminus\{0\}\) is primitive.  Choose a coordinate
\(i\in\{1,2\}\) with \(v_i\neq0\).  The integers \(a_i+kv_i\) are distinct.
For every positive-volume point of the coset, put \(s=a_i+kv_i\).  Then
\[
-20\leq s\leq20,
\qquad
\|a+kv\|_\infty\geq |s|,
\]
so (3) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{z\in(a+\mathbb Zv)\cap\mathbb Z^2}w_z
&\leq
\omega_{10}
\sum_{s=-20}^{20}(21-|s|)^{10}\\
&=
\omega_{10}\overline L,
\end{aligned}
\tag{7}
\]
where
\[
\overline L
:=
21^{10}+2\sum_{j=1}^{20}j^{10}
=65007024339901.
\]
The exact difference
\[
\overline W-2\overline L
=321466537773199>0
\tag{8}
\]
proves the required strict inequality
\[
\sum_{z\in(a+\mathbb Zv)\cap\mathbb Z^2}w_z<\frac W2
\]
for every primitive line coset.  Empty cosets have zero mass.

The positive support has convex hull
\[
\operatorname{conv}D=[-20,20]^2,
\]
so \(0\in\operatorname{int}\operatorname{conv}D\), and \(w_0>0\).
Moreover, \(w_z=w_{-z}\).  Let \(Q\subsetneq\mathbb R^2\) be any closed
halfspace containing \(0\).  Write
\[
Q=\{z:u^\top z\geq b\},
\qquad
u\neq0,\quad b\leq0.
\]
Then
\[
Q_0:=\{z:u^\top z\geq0\}\subseteq Q.
\]
Pairing every \(z\) with \(-z\) shows that \(Q_0\) contains at least one
member of every pair, while it contains both members of a pair lying on its
boundary.  Therefore
\[
\sum_{z\in Q\cap\mathbb Z^2}w_z
\geq
\sum_{z\in Q_0\cap\mathbb Z^2}w_z
\geq\frac W2>\frac W4.
\tag{9}
\]
Thus \(0\) is a qualifying marginal centerpoint, with room beyond the
registered threshold.

It remains to compute the strict parity threshold.  For
\(r=(r_1,r_2)\in(\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z)^2\), write
\[
W_r=\omega_{10}\overline W_r.
\]
On the shell \(\|z\|_\infty=m\), the four parity counts are
\[
\begin{array}{c|cccc}
&00&01&10&11\\ \hline
m\ {\rm even}&4m&2m&2m&0\\
m\ {\rm odd}&0&2m&2m&4m.
\end{array}
\tag{10}
\]
The anchor has parity \(00\).  Hence direct finite summation gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\overline W_{00}
&=
21^{10}
+\sum_{\substack{1\leq m\leq20\\m\ {\rm even}}}
4m(21-m)^{10}
=117456705062801,\\
\overline W_{01}
=\overline W_{10}
&=
\sum_{m=1}^{20}2m(21-m)^{10}
=108700176368700,\\
\overline W_{11}
&=
\sum_{\substack{1\leq m\leq20\\m\ {\rm odd}}}
4m(21-m)^{10}
=116623528652800.
\end{aligned}
\tag{11}
\]
Their sum is the value \(\overline W\) in (4).  The diagonal square mass is
\[
\sum_z w_z^2
=\omega_{10}^2\overline D,
\]
\[
\overline D
:=
21^{20}
+8\sum_{m=1}^{20}m(21-m)^{20}
=2225091831194892164707306209.
\tag{12}
\]
Consequently,
\[
Q^\circ=\omega_{10}^2\overline Q,
\]
\[
\begin{aligned}
\overline Q
&:=
\overline W_{00}^2
+2\overline W_{01}^2
+\overline W_{11}^2
-\overline D\\
&=
48803489853618364320273879392.
\end{aligned}
\tag{13}
\]
The exact integer certificate
\[
256\overline Q-16\overline W^2
=9232337883423169904672002628336>0
\tag{14}
\]
shows that
\[
Q^\circ>\frac1{16}W^2
>\frac{16-e}{256}W^2.
\tag{15}
\]
This verifies the registered strict off-diagonal threshold without an
asymptotic estimate.

We finally compute the complete support-safe score at \(z_0=0\).  Put
\[
\gamma:=\left(\frac{10}{11}\right)^{10},
\qquad
q:=(1-\gamma)^{1/10}.
\]
The exact integer inequality
\[
\begin{aligned}
&11^{10}21^{10}
-10^{10}21^{10}
-20^{10}11^{10}\\
&\hspace{25mm}
=235117529492562122801>0
\end{aligned}
\tag{16}
\]
is equivalent to
\[
1-\left(\frac{10}{11}\right)^{10}
>
\left(\frac{20}{21}\right)^{10}.
\]
Thus
\[
q>\frac{20}{21}.
\tag{17}
\]

Let \(v\in\mathbb Z^2\setminus\{0\}\), and put
\[
m:=\|v\|_\infty.
\]
The two fibers symmetric about \(0\) have equal root volumes.  If
\(1\leq m\leq20\), their roots are
\[
A=B=\omega_{10}^{1/10}(21-m)
\leq20\omega_{10}^{1/10}.
\]
At the anchor,
\[
R_0=w_0^{1/10}=21\omega_{10}^{1/10},
\qquad
S_0=2qR_0.
\]
By (17),
\[
A+B
\leq40\omega_{10}^{1/10}
<
42q\omega_{10}^{1/10}
=S_0.
\tag{18}
\]
When \(m\geq21\), both endpoint volumes are zero.  In every case the capped
maximum in the definition of \(\Phi_{10,S_0}(A,B)\) equals
\(A^{10}+B^{10}\), so
\[
\Phi_{10,S_0}(A,B)=0,
\qquad
\Psi_{10,S_0}(A,B)=0.
\tag{19}
\]
This treats every unordered symmetric pair, including all zero-volume
endpoints.

It follows that the entire pair sum vanishes and
\[
\mathcal E^\Psi_{10}(w;0)
=\gamma w_0
=
\omega_{10}\frac{10^{10}21^{10}}{11^{10}}.
\tag{20}
\]
The final exact integer certificate is
\[
11^{10}\overline W
-64\cdot10^{10}21^{10}
=1035119843891335467677601>0.
\tag{21}
\]
Multiplying the desired comparison by
\(\omega_{10}/(64\cdot11^{10})>0\), equation (21) gives exactly
\[
\mathcal E^\Psi_{10}(w;0)<\frac W{64}.
\tag{22}
\]

For calibration, the mixed-volume measure of (1) is centrally symmetric
about \((0,0)\).  Every closed halfspace containing \((0,0)\) therefore has
mixed mass at least \(W/2\).  The halfspace
\[
\{(z,x):x_1\geq0\}
\]
bisects every positive-volume Euclidean-ball fiber and has mixed mass
exactly \(W/2\).  Hence
\[
h_{C\cap(\mathbb Z^2\times\mathbb R^{10})}((0,0))
=\frac W2.
\]
The counterexample refutes only the registered support-safe profile-energy
completion.  Its `target_match` must be `null`.
statement:
Let \(d=10\), write \(z=(z_1,z_2)\in\mathbb R^2\) and
\(x\in\mathbb R^{10}\), and define
\[
C:=
\left\{(z,x)\in\mathbb R^{12}:
\|z\|_\infty+\|x\|_2\leq21
\right\}.
\tag{1}
\]
Let
\[
\omega_{10}:=\operatorname{vol}_{10}(B_2^{10})=\frac{\pi^5}{120},
\qquad z_0:=0.
\]
Then \(C\) is a compact full-dimensional convex body.  Its complete
positive lattice-fiber profile is
\[
D:=\{z\in\mathbb Z^2:w_z>0\}
=[-20,20]^2\cap\mathbb Z^2,
\tag{2}
\]
\[
C_z=(21-\|z\|_\infty)B_2^{10},
\qquad
w_z=\omega_{10}(21-\|z\|_\infty)^{10}
\quad(z\in D),
\tag{3}
\]
and \(w_z=0\) for every \(z\notin D\).  Its total mixed volume is
\[
W=\omega_{10}\overline W,
\qquad
\overline W
:=
21^{10}
+8\sum_{m=1}^{20}m(21-m)^{10}
=451480586453001.
\tag{4}
\]
This body and \(z_0\) satisfy every hypothesis of
`n2-support-safe-energy`, but
\[
\mathcal E^\Psi_{10}(w;0)
=
\left(\frac{10}{11}\right)^{10}w_0
<
\frac W{64}.
\tag{5}
\]
Thus the registered exact profile inequality is disproved.  This is not a
counterexample to the locked weak Oertel statement: the actual mixed depth
at \((0,0)\) is \(W/2\).
